clue.text: Health food

definitions.meaning: drunk to someone's health, so the word can stand for that salute
... bread is an everyday breakfast food

explanation.surface: A one-line note on wholesome eating, as if from a diet column.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink raised to someone's good health is a toast; grilled bread is also toast.

clue.text: Can barristers get shut inside historic building?

indicators.note: get shut inside says the barristers are enclosed within the can word

parts.note: a tin is a can
the Bar is the collective name for barristers

explanation.surface: Can lawyers be locked in an old building?
explanation.walkthrough: 'get shut inside' puts THE BAR inside TIN. A tithe barn was a medieval barn where a tenth of farm produce was stored as church tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn is a large medieval barn, many surviving as historic buildings.

clue.text: Crudely engrave "Nemesis"

indicators.note: crudely means roughly, so the letters of the next word are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Roughly carve the word Nemesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crudely' signals an anagram of ENGRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, so she is an avenger.

clue.text: Connection that is hidden in container

indicators.note: hidden in says the abbreviation is concealed inside the container word

parts.note: a tin is a container
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A link, i.e., kept out of sight in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: Despite 'hidden in', this is not a run of the clue's letters: 'hidden in' works as a container signal, the abbreviation sitting inside the container word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a link or association between two things.

clue.text: Straying into out-of-the-way retreat, exhibiting audacity

indicators.note: into says the straying word is placed inside the other piece
to retreat is to go backwards, so the word for out-of-the-way is read in reverse

parts.note: an out-of-the-way place can be called odd, i.e. unusual or remote
straying means erring, going astray

explanation.surface: Someone wandering into a remote hideaway shows great daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks like a noun (a hideaway) but works as the reversal signal, giving DDO; 'into' then splits it after the first D.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is old-fashioned heroic daring, a synonym for audacity.

clue.text: Topside carved up and put down

indicators.note: carved up means cut into pieces, so the letters of the joint are rearranged

explanation.surface: A joint of topside beef is sliced and set on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved up' signals an anagram of TOPSIDE, a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit something is to put it down or lay it somewhere.

clue.text: Spite given vocal expression in private

indicators.note: given vocal expression means spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier serving in the ranks, such as a private

explanation.surface: Malice voiced behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, without the final R sounded, 'ranker' and 'rancour' sound alike. 'In private' looks like 'in secret' but 'private' is the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, lasting resentment, which is close to spite.

clue.text: Working together during performance

definitions.meaning: while a concert is happening, live on stage

explanation.surface: A musician's note about playing together while on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: In concert means acting together in harmony, and literally it means at a concert.

clue.text: Part of ship providing hitman with a drink

parts.note: a gun is slang for a hired gunman or hitman
ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A ship's part supplies a hired killer with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of the side of a ship or boat.

clue.text: Where chalk may be put at the right moment

definitions.meaning: snooker players rub chalk on the tip of their stick
exactly when required, like an actor responding to a prompt

explanation.surface: A billiards tip about chalk and good timing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalk goes literally on a snooker cue; the idiom means happening at just the right time.

clue.text: Revamp hut and reopen immediately after that

indicators.note: to revamp is to rework, so the letters of the two following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shed is renovated and opens its doors again straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revamp' signals an anagram of HUT plus REOPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereupon is a formal adverb meaning directly following that, at once.

clue.text: Fancy niche accommodating one with little faith in human nature

definitions.text: one with little faith in human nature

indicators.note: accommodating means holding within, so the answer is found inside the two words

explanation.surface: An ornate alcove houses a pessimist about humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' tells you the answer is housed in 'fanCY NICHe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic is a person who distrusts people's motives and expects the worst of them.

clue.text: Aged person can go running in this track event

indicators.note: running means moving about, so the letters of the four words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly competitor may take part in this athletics race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' signals an anagram of AGED PERSON CAN GO. The surface fits too: a gentle novelty race at a British school sports day where runners balance an egg on a spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg-and-spoon race is a novelty sports-day race run on a track.

clue.text: Bill has drum sent round for circus artiste

parts.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill

indicators.note: sent round means turned about, so the drum's name is read backwards

parts.note: a tabor is a small drum

explanation.surface: A man called Bill brings a drum on a circuit for a circus performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is the account abbreviation; 'sent round' gives ROBAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat is a gymnastic performer, a staple act in a circus.

clue.text: Runs have to be inside rail for large animal

indicators.note: inside says the first pieces go within the rail word

parts.note: a bar is a rail
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to own is to have
taken as written

explanation.surface: Runs must stay within the rail for some big beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' tempts as a verb but is the cricket abbreviation, and 'to' is just a link inside 'have to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: The brown bear is a large species of bear, so an example of a large animal.

clue.text: Most of page covers fish put back in

indicators.note: covers means goes round, so the shortened page word wraps the fish
most of means the last letter of the page word is dropped

parts.note: a recto is a right-hand page of a book
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Most of a page is taken up with a fish that has been returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' leaves RECT, which 'covers' the fish, wrapping it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elect is to vote someone back into office, putting them back in.

clue.text: Fail to take advantage of underemphasised line

definitions.meaning: a remark delivered casually, without emphasis

explanation.surface: An actor's regret at wasting a line by underplaying it.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw away is to squander a chance; a throwaway is a line spoken offhandedly.

clue.text: Poet in renovated bar

parts.note: something renovated is made like new
a bolt is a bar that secures a door

explanation.surface: A poet is found in a newly done-up pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Newbolt was an English poet known for 'Drake's Drum'. 'Bar' suggests a pub but means a door bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Newbolt was an English poet, so his surname is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Lexicographer reveals way composer's taken in

indicators.note: taken in means absorbed, so the way word goes inside the composer

parts.note: Carl Maria von Weber was a German composer
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A dictionary-maker reveals a route a composer has followed.
explanation.walkthrough: Weber was a German Romantic composer; Noah Webster compiled the first great American dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah Webster compiled the first major American English dictionary, so he is an example of a lexicographer.

clue.text: Bolshevik's wrong, upset over weather

definitions.note: the 's is short for 'is', so the definition reads as a person

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upward, so the wrong is read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the sky stands for the weather, as in clear skies

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is mistaken and annoyed about the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives TROT, sitting over the weather word in this down answer; 'over' is positional.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was a leading Bolshevik revolutionary, an example of the type.

clue.text: Baseball player booked in the rye

definitions.meaning: the fielder behind home plate in baseball
the figure placed in the rye in the title of Salinger's novel

explanation.surface: A ballplayer has a reservation in a field of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked' means in a book's title: Salinger's novel 'The Catcher in the Rye'.
explanation.definitionFit: The baseball player crouching behind the batter is the catcher; Salinger's title names one in the rye.

clue.text: Will's rider police set up in a twist

indicators.note: in says the police abbreviation goes inside the twist word

parts.note: a coil is a twist

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised, so the police letters are read upwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: Officers concoct a twisted addition to a will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' gives DIC, the police letters read upwards in this down answer; 'rider' means an added clause, not a horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplement that modifies a will, a rider added to it.

clue.text: Happy chappie caught in cabin

indicators.note: in says the fellow and the catch go inside the cabin word

parts.note: a hut is a cabin
Alf is a typical name for a chap
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cheerful fellow is caught inside a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' is slang for tipsy, the sense of the answer; Alf is a stock crossword name for any chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, and happy can mean pleasantly tipsy.

clue.text: Dressing old man in order to see off daughter — a mischievous one

parts.note: robing means dressing, putting on robes

indicators.note: to see off is to get rid of, so a letter is removed from the man's title

parts.note: an Oddfellow is a member of the Independent Order of Oddfellows, a friendly society

explanation.surface: An old man dresses up to wave his daughter goodbye, being a rascal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see off' removes one D from ODDFELLOW, leaving ODFELLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is Puck, the impish sprite of English folklore famed for pranks.

clue.text: Approach formed quickly

definitions.meaning: the period or path leading up to something
made in haste, as when sewing a garment swiftly

explanation.surface: A tailor's note about a quickly made garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach to an event; to run up something is to make it fast.

clue.text: People retained by newspaper boss to make corrections

indicators.note: retained by means kept inside, so the people go within the boss word

parts.note: ED is short for editor
men are people

explanation.surface: Staff kept on by an editor to fix errors.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct and improve a text.

clue.text: Two elements turned into saltpetre

indicators.note: turned means reversed, so both element names are read backwards together

parts.note: Er is the chemical symbol for erbium
tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: Two chemical elements are converted into saltpetre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses ER + TIN as a whole to give the answer. Fittingly, saltpetre is itself a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is another name for saltpetre, potassium nitrate.

clue.text: Worried in case crowd find something above criticism

indicators.note: worried means troubled or shaken about, so the letters of the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Anxious in case the crowd finds something beyond reproach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' signals an anagram of CASE CROWD.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idiom for an institution or idea treated as immune from criticism.

clue.text: Depiction of light coming in the doorway

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the light goes inside the doorway word

parts.note: a portal is a doorway or gateway
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A picture of light streaming in through the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a representation, a synonym for depiction.

clue.text: Spotted bats

explanation.surface: A two-word field note: some bats were sighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty means covered with dots, and informally it means mildly mad, like bats.
